**Aliases:** A=`aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` (#12 pre-rework), B=`bbbb…` (#13), C=`cccc…` (#14), R=`2222222222222222222222222222222222222222` (Rework base), E=`eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee` (final HEAD).

The home PR is #12, https://github.com/acme/widget/pull/12. It is OPEN, its head is `retry` and its base is `main`. `PRE_REWORK_HEAD`=A.

## Preflight (rebase mode: `Rework base:` recorded)
```bash
git -C "$WORKTREE" fetch origin
git -C "$WORKTREE" merge-base --is-ancestor 2222222222222222222222222222222222222222 HEAD   # exit 0
git -C "$WORKTREE" rev-parse origin/retry                                                    # = A
```
`origin/retry` equals A, so the push uses a lease. Row 1 is offered and was chosen.

## Preparation order (row 1)
1. **Capture evidence.** Record the scoped set `test-retry` and the accepted-complete task and thread evidence.
2. **Refetch threads.** Run the paginated `pr-head` query once each with `n=12`, `n=13` and `n=14`.
   - #12 HOME is recorded `keep open`, so it resolves to `still open`.
   - #13 MEMBER13 keeps its recorded member disposition. Member history proves it, never home's first-parent history.
   - #13 NEW13 is newly opened, so it resolves to `still open`.
   - #14 MEMBER14 is recorded `keep open`, so it resolves to `still open`.
3. **Strip and seal.** Run the plan-strip loop, then:
   ```bash
   node <bin>/gauntlet-telemetry-seal.mjs --worktree "$WORKTREE" --option pr --base origin/main --spec doc/specs/rework.md
   ```
   Print its stdout verbatim. A nonzero exit stops the flow here.
4. **Probe refs.** Run `git -C "$WORKTREE" rev-parse -q --verify refs/gauntlet/pre-rework/pr-12` and the same for `pr-13` and `pr-14`. All three exist, so they are preserved and no `update-ref` runs.

## Push (home only)
```bash
git -C "$WORKTREE" push --no-follow-tags --force-with-lease=retry:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa origin HEAD:refs/heads/retry
```
The push succeeded. The pushed home head is E.

## Body FETCH
```bash
gh pr view 12 -R acme/widget --json body
BODY=$(mktemp)   # outside the repo
```
- Decode the JSON `body` exactly, with no trimming and no `$(...)` capture.
- Write those bytes, `Original description\n`, to `$BODY`.
- Append one blank line (`\n`), then the block below.

The resulting file starts with `Original description\n\n## Rework\n…`.

## Rework block
```markdown
## Rework

Before: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa (local ref `refs/gauntlet/pre-rework/pr-12` in the rework checkout)
Absorbs: #13 (https://github.com/acme/widget/pull/13), #14 (https://github.com/acme/widget/pull/14)
Spec: doc/specs/rework.md at eeeeeee
Keeps: retry API
Changes: repair retry
Dropped claims: none
Verification: scoped - test-retry; CI on this push holds the full run. Telemetry: whole PR against main.
Threads:
#12:
- HOME - still open
#13:
- MEMBER13 - fix - retain delay (recorded member disposition; member history)
- NEW13 - still open
#14:
- MEMBER14 - still open
```
The original claims were not all dropped, so the block has no `supersedes the description above` line.

## Body EDIT
```bash
gh pr edit 12 -R acme/widget --body-file "$BODY"
```
The edit succeeded. Member eligibility and closure come next, at the separate close-absorbed-PRs gate. Ship is not marked complete yet.

### Shared preparation

SHA aliases: `A=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` (#12), `B=bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb` (#13), `C=cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc` (#14), `R=2222222222222222222222222222222222222222` (rework base), `H=eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee` (final/pushed HEAD).

Synthetic checkpoint only; execute nothing.

1. Retain `test-retry`, accepted-complete task/thread evidence, and all recorded PR identities before stripping.
2. Run rebase-mode preflight:

```bash
WORKTREE=/work/widget/.worktrees/retry
git -C "$WORKTREE" fetch origin
git -C "$WORKTREE" merge-base --is-ancestor "$R" HEAD
git -C "$WORKTREE" rev-parse origin/retry
```

Require fetch success, ancestry exit 0, and resolved origin SHA equal to `$A`. This selects the explicit lease push. Do **not** test original-head ancestry against rebased HEAD.

3. Refresh all three PRs’ threads using the prescribed paginated query and comment pagination. Retain member dispositions, add `NEW13` as still open, and never infer member fixes from home’s first-parent history.
4. Read the artifact’s `**Spec:**` header; resolve plan directories through `flowGuards`. Remove tracked paired task-plan and ledger candidates, committing each removal as `Remove ephemeral plan doc`. Preserve the spec and telemetry.
5. Seal, stopping on nonzero exit:

```bash
node <bin>/gauntlet-telemetry-seal.mjs \
  --worktree "$WORKTREE" --option pr \
  --base origin/main --spec doc/specs/rework.md
```

Retain actual seal stdout verbatim for eventual completion; no synthetic outcome is assumed.

6. Probe existing refs; preserve them without rewriting:

```bash
git -C "$WORKTREE" rev-parse -q --verify refs/gauntlet/pre-rework/pr-12
git -C "$WORKTREE" rev-parse -q --verify refs/gauntlet/pre-rework/pr-13
git -C "$WORKTREE" rev-parse -q --verify refs/gauntlet/pre-rework/pr-14
```

7. Push home only:

```bash
git -C "$WORKTREE" push --no-follow-tags \
  --force-with-lease=retry:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa \
  origin HEAD:refs/heads/retry
git -C "$WORKTREE" rev-parse HEAD
```

Save `$H` after successful push.

The one place After is weaker than Before is the body FETCH: it shows `gh pr view 12 -R acme/widget --json body` with no redirection and then describes the byte handling in prose ("decode exactly, no trimming, no `$(...)` capture"), whereas Before showed the actual pipeline (`> "$JSON"`, `jq -j '.body' < "$JSON" > "$BODY"`, `printf '\n' >> "$BODY"`, heredoc append). Since the case explicitly asks for exact FETCH and EDIT calls with byte handling, keep Before's concrete redirect/jq/printf sequence in After while retaining After's literal full-SHA lease and `--repo`/`-R` edit call; that wording satisfies every conjunct of ordering without ambiguity and still delivers the Change. Attribution is unchanged and correct in both: Absorbs lists #13/#14 with literal URLs, threads are grouped under #12/#13/#14, MEMBER13's recorded fix disposition is attributed to member history (not home first-parent), and NEW13 appears as still open.
